# Problem 1

```{r message=FALSE}
library(p8105.datasets)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

data("ny_noaa")
```

```{r include=FALSE}
skimr::skim(ny_noaa)
```

## NY NOAA Data Description

1. The `ny_noaa` dataset contains 2,595,176 daily observations from 747 stations (1981–2010), with seven variables: `id`, `date`, `prcp`, `snow`, `snwd`, `tmax`, and `tmin`.

2. Missing rates are highest for `tmax` and `tmin` (43.71% each), followed by `snwd` (22.80%), `snow` (14.69%), and `prcp` (5.62%). Station IDs and dates are complete.


## Data Cleaning

```{r}
ny_noaa_clean =
  ny_noaa |>
  separate(
    date,
    into = c("year", "month", "day"),
    sep = "-",
    remove = FALSE,
    convert = TRUE
  ) |>
  mutate(
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10,
    snow = snow / 10,
    snwd = snwd / 10
  )
```

```{r include=FALSE}
ny_noaa_clean |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(10)
```

1. The date was separated into numeric `year`, `month`, and `day` variables. Temperatures were converted to degrees Celsius, precipitation to millimeters, and snowfall and snow depth to centimeters.

2. The most common value is 0 cm. Common positive values include 1.3, 2.5, and 5.1 cm, consistent with measurements in approximate half-inch and whole-inch increments.


## Average Maximum Temperatures

```{r}
monthly_tmax_df =
  ny_noaa_clean |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) |>
  drop_na(tmax) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax),
    n_days = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c(1, 7),
      labels = c("January", "July")
    )
  )

monthly_tmax_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .25, size = .7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Maximum Temperature by Station and Year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Mean maximum temperature (C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

1. January is substantially colder than July. Mean maximum temperatures vary across stations and years.

2. Some station-year averages are extreme, including approximately -13.4°C in January and 33.6°C in July. These values should be examined alongside the number of recorded days.
